newsitem.title: USA: Unimed's NTZ gets expanded orphan status.
newsitem.headline: Unimed's NTZ gets expanded orphan status.

text.p: Unimed Pharmaceuticals Inc said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration expanded the Orphan Drug designation for nitazoxanide, or NTZ, to cover immune-compromised patients with cryptosporidiosis.
The compound's prior designation was limited to treating cryptosporidiosis in HIV positive and AIDS patients.
Orphan Drug designation is reserved for conditions that affect fewer than 200,000 patients, Unimed said.
If NTZ were approved for treating cryptosporidiosis in HIV positive and AIDS other immune-compromised patients, Unimed would get seven years' marketing exclusivity and tax credits.
The compound will begin its final phase of clinical trials immediately, Unimed said.

There is no consistently effective or approved therapy for cryptosporidiosis, a condition caused by a protozoan parasite that can cause profuse diarrhea, abdominal cramping, urgency, severe dehydration and weight loss.

It is estimated that 15-20 percent of AIDS patients suffer from cryptosporidiosis, Unimed said. Other patients who can suffer the disorder include the elderly, cancer patients, and transplant patients.

NTZ is a nitrothiazole benzamide compound that can combat a number of pathogens. Unimed holds an exclusive license to develop and market oral dosage formulations of NTZ for human use in the United States, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand from Romark Laboratories LC.
